To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gating residue Asp137 controls peroxidatic activation and catalytic turnover of the anti-tb pro-drug isonicotinohydrazide by the mycobacterium tuberculosis KatG.
access channel residues Ser315, Asp137 and Ser139 in M. tuberculosis catalase-perioxidase control peroxidatic catalytic activation of the anti-TB pro-drug isoni-azid.
access channel gating residues Ser315 and Aspartate137 in Mycobacterial catalase-peroxidases (KatG) regulate peroxidatic activation and the subsequent inactivation of isoniazid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the catalase-peroxidases from M. tuberculosis and the human pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
the mechanism of peroxidatic activation and the gating residues of the heme access channel in KatG.
the structural basis of peroxidatic activation, the role of the gating residues, and the structural basis of resistance to isoniazid in Mycobacterum tuberculosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gating residues Ser315 and Asn137 are essential to regulate the access of substrates and products to the heme site.
Asp137 is a gating residue in KatG that controls the access of substrates to the catalytic center.
the bottleneck of the channel is too narrow for isoniazid to enter the heme active site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the access channel of KatG is an important determinant of the catalytic efficiency and substrate specificity of this enzyme.
the access channel residues Ser315, Ser137, and Arg139 are critical for the peroxidatic activation reaction.
the bottleneck of the channel is not the rate limiting step for isoniazid activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

gating residues Ser315 and Asn137 control the rate-limiting step in the peroxidatic activation pathway of isoniazid, and that this control is exerted by a steric restriction at a bottleneck of the heme access channel.

the bottleneck of the heme access channel of M. tuberculosis KatG, which has a Ser residue at this position, is not as restrictive as the bottleneck of the corresponding channel in Escherichia coli KatG, which is a Tyr residue.
the bottleneck of the access channel is the key structural element that controls the gating of the channel and thereby the peroxidatic activity of KatG.
